summary_en: This phase III trial compares radiation with cetuximab to radiation with carboplatin and paclitaxel in adults with locally advanced head and neck squamous cell cancer who cannot receive cisplatin. Intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) is given 5 days per week for 35 treatments, and cetuximab or carboplatin and paclitaxel is given intravenously on day 1 of each 7-day cycle for up to 7 cycles, if the disease does not progress and side effects are acceptable. The main outcome is not stated; the record lists this as a phase 3 trial.
summary_es: Este ensayo de fase III compara radioterapia con cetuximab frente a radioterapia con carboplatino y paclitaxel en adultos con cáncer de cabeza y cuello de células escamosas localmente avanzado que no pueden recibir cisplatino. La radioterapia de intensidad modulada (IMRT) se administra 5 días por semana durante 35 tratamientos, y el cetuximab o el carboplatino con paclitaxel se administran por vía intravenosa el día 1 de cada ciclo de 7 días, hasta 7 ciclos, si la enfermedad no progresa y los efectos secundarios son aceptables. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el registro señala que este es un ensayo de fase 3.
who_for: Previously untreated, unresected squamous cell cancer of the larynx, hypopharynx, oropharynx, or oral cavity
Locally advanced disease at AJCC 9th edition stage II to IVB, depending on site and p16 status
Contraindication to cisplatin, such as creatinine clearance under 60 mL/min, grade 2 or higher nerve damage, or hearing loss
Age 70 or older with HNCIG omega score under 0.80, or under 70 with omega under 0.80, Charlson score of at least 1, and G-8 score of 14 or less
Age 18 or older, and not pregnant or nursing
not_for: Prior systemic therapy for this head and neck cancer
Prior radiation to the same region that would overlap with the planned radiation fields
Prior surgery for this head and neck cancer
Cannot safely receive the radiation and drug regimens per FDA labeling and investigator judgment
cancer_types: head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
